Given $f \in C([0,1]^d)$, there exist affine maps $\mathcal{A}_{i},\, \mathcal{A}_{i}^{\mathrm{out}} \in \aff_{\le 5d}$ for all $i\in\mathbb{N}^+$ such that the sequence of multigrade approximations

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims a guarantee that grade-wise training, i.e., the per-grade optimization problems formulated in Section 2.1, yields vanishing approximation error. What the paper actually establishes (Theorems 1.1 and 3.1) is the existence of an analytically constructed sequence of grade-wise blocks whose residuals vanish. No result shows that solving the grade-wise optimization problems, or any training dynamics, produces or approximates such blocks; the conclusion itself concedes that the learned-from-data case is open.

failure_location.quote: To the best of our knowledge, this work provides the first rigorous theoretical guarantee that grade-wise training yields provable vanishing approximation error in deep networks.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rephrase the abstract, introduction, and conclusion claims to state that there exists a grade-wise multigrade ReLU construction with vanishing residuals, removing assertions that the training procedure yields it.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised guarantee concerns scheme existence (approximation theory), not trainability; readers are told the MGDL training procedure provably converges, which is not established.
issues.title: Headline claim that grade-wise training yields vanishing error overstates the proven existence result
issues.why_classification: A local prose correction; all formal results and their statements are unaffected.

The invoked one-step contraction (Theorem 3.1) is only established for eps in (0, 1/(1+2^d)): the operator T_eps is defined only under that restriction (the factor 1 - eps - 2^d eps must be positive), and the proof of Theorem 1.1 constructs the checkpoints by applying Theorem 3.1 with the prescribed eps. issues.failure_explanation: The theorem places no restriction on f, so f identically 0 is admissible. Then f_1 = f is identically 0 and the claimed strict inequality at k=1 reads ||f_2||_{L^p} < ||f_1||_{L^p} = 0, impossible for any choice of maps. The construction itself degenerates (M_f = M_{-f} = 0, so T_eps f = 0 and T_eps(-f) = 0, no cubes are selected, n = 0), contradicting the claimed n in N^+. Hence Theorem 3.1(iii) is false as stated for the zero target. Correspondingly, the proof of Theorem 1.1, whose first step applies Theorem 3.1 to f, breaks down for f identically 0 (Theorem 1.1's own statement can still be met for this input by a separate construction, e.g., Phi_k = c_k Gamma with c_k strictly decreasing to 0).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that f is not identically zero to Theorem 3.1 (or weaken (iii) to hold only while f_k is not identically zero), and handle the zero target in Theorem 1.1 by a short separate construction.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 3.1(iii) fails on the degenerate input f = 0, and the iterative proof of Theorem 1.1 (and Corollary 1.2) is invalid for that input.
issues.title: Theorem 3.1(iii) is impossible for the identically zero target
issues.why_classification: A degenerate-case exclusion plus a short separate argument preserves every substantive claim, rate, and advertised scope.

The claim is in fact true (e.g., via states (x, phi_k) in R^{5d} that carry the input through the ReLU layers, valid since x in [0,1]^d is nonnegative, with each layer computing its own 4d trapezoid features and each A_k^out reading out h_k affinely), but this construction is absent from the paper.

issues.failure_explanation: The sketch asserts the construction yields a pointwise multiplicative contraction |g - Sg| <= (1-eps)|g| for all x. It does not: at any point where g > 0 is small or moderate but which lies outside all dilated cubes, Sg = 0 (cf. eq:Tg:outside) and the asserted inequality fails. Concrete counterexample: d = 1, g(x) = 1 - 0.9x on [0,1], eps = 0.1; at x = 0.9 the construction gives Sg = 0 and |g - Sg| = 0.19 > 0.171 = (1-eps)|g|. What the construction actually provides is the pointwise domination |Sg| <= |g| (condition (C1)) together with the L^infinity norm contraction; the formal proof of Theorem 3.1 uses only these, so no formal result depends on the false pointwise estimate.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds the drop of g between x-tilde in E_{g,eps} and x in rQ by omega_{g^+}(2 sqrt(d) delta), but the modulus of continuity of g^+ controls only the variation of g^+, which can be much smaller than that of g (a steep dive of g below zero is invisible to g^+). The inference is invalid as written. The intended conclusion (g >= 2^d eps M_g on A_{g,eps}, eq. (g:lower)) is nevertheless true: since g(x-tilde) = g^+(x-tilde) >= (1-eps)M_g, the modulus bound gives g^+(x) >= 2^d eps M_g > 0, whence g(x) = g^+(x). The same sloppiness affects Stage II's justification of strict L^p monotonicity via the claim 'h_k > 0 on the cube Q_hat_k subset Omega_1' (the grid cube can exit [0,1]^d; only its intersection with the domain lies in Omega_1, via this same lower-bound estimate).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Route the estimate through g^+: replace g by g^+ in the two displayed terms and conclude via g^+(x) >= 2^d eps M_g > 0 implying g(x) = g^+(x); similarly justify the Stage II support claim via rQ_hat_k intersect [0,1]^d being contained in Omega_1.
issues.overall_effect: The key lower-bound estimate behind condition (C1), and hence the positive-contraction lemma, Theorem 3.1, Theorem 1.1, and Corollary 1.2, rests on an unjustified step as written.
